trans-unit.source: The hottest place in the System. Vulco's tidal locking to Juno makes this face as hot as you can get without touching its parent star. The floor is lava is not a joke anymore.
The large stresses in Vulco result in lava flows running front to back, resulting in some of the most impressive terrain features in the entire System.
Being tidally locked to a star makes one face crazy hot and the other crazy cold. This rift hasn't seen Juno's light in eons.
You won't find Cerberus in this ravine, but Hell's Gate can show you what looking at the heart of a planet through its crust looks like.
The largest active volcano in the system, very steep and hard to climb, but even harder to escape once you descend into its crater.
The mountains near Hathor Mons formed from one of the volcano's eruptions. They offer easier-to-climb terrain and a great viewing spot to plan your descent into the crater.
Sergeaa has a large portion of its surface covered in large obsidian spikes, three of which form a large crown surrounded by some of the most surreal panoramas.
This volcano has been dormant for millennia, but its crater is almost intact. It may have no lava inside, but descending to its bottom and coming back intact can still be a challenge.
A crescent-moon-shaped island at the edge of one of Sergeaa's largest lava lakes, hell's version of Hawaii, surrounded by magma and obsidian spikes.
A strip of sand surrounded by lakes and mountains inside a chain of craters.
A series of red steep peaks ripping through the ground like claws.
Ripples in the surface, mountain sized waves of dust and rock.
Some say it is a bottomless pit, but it is just a really deep hole.
A conveniently placed barge to try to land your rocket boosters when launching from the DSC.
Every explorer's dream, the South Pole. You won't find Santa Claus here, but its very flat terrain can be great for landspeed records.
Where the rainforest meets the desert, only stopped by one of the most spectacular mountain systems on Droo.
Fresh grass, swirly mountains and a bright Juno, the perfect spot for any hiker wanting to get lost.
The smell of the ocean, the water's roar, a cold breeze hitting your face in the smallest island of the largest archipelago on Droo.
Your last chance to touch solid terrain before reaching the icebergs on your way to the South Pole — even if it's entirely covered in snow.
Believed to result from whatever caused T.T. to orbit Droo. It resembles the Death Star, but this crater doesn't shoot lasers. Or does it?
When the Mimas Crater was formed, a lot of ejecta fell back to Brigo, forming a series of rings around it that resulted on large cliffs.
A system of mountains covered in ice and mud, definitely not chocolate icecream.
A cliff looking at mares that reaches as far as the eye can see, with nothing but volcanic rock and craters ahead.
Luna can go from very rough terrain to flatlands really fast, resulting in impressive cliffs. Sometimes these cliffs can break apart, resulting in Simple Rocks Too.
Sometimes a crater's scale isn't apparent from afar. Only inside do you realize how small you are. These are the real 'deep' space industries.
A mountain generated after a great impact that left one of the largest craters in this moon's surface.
This strange outer space boulder is covered in oxides, making its very rough surface have a tint that resembles that of blood.
T.T. shows clear signs of having been through an intense event, because its surface is partially melted, and parts of its metallic core are entirely exposed.
A mountain right on the edge of the largest ravine in Cylero, one of the most unique viewpoints to visit while exploring this rare Landmark.
The largest mountain in the Juno System was once a fiery volcano, now completely dormant. Inside its crater, you can only imagine the insane power this behemoth once had.
A small peak on the edge of one of the arms of the Northern Polar Swirl, looking straight into one of the valleys formed by it.
Although rare, impacts can sometimes happen in the exact same place. Here, a small asteroid cleared the central uplifts of a large crater's central plane.
The volcano marking Nebra's origin, where the main meridian meets its equator. Small but powerful — you may never leave its crater if you aren't careful.
Nebra's very high volcanic activity formed a ring of volcanic islands, one of the best spots for a land base on this moon.
A volcano with a collapsed crater that now resembles a teapot. I could swear I saw it up in the sky, green as an emerald in the blue; now I'm wondering if it was really you.
If Nebra's water temperature wasn't enough of a problem for you, the Litke Basin adds total darkness and abyssal pressures to the mix.
A terrace in the side of the largest mountain in Taurus looking into one of the most extreme valleys in the Juno system.
A very thin and tall mesa at the end of the longest depression, surrounded by cliffs from all directions except the entrance of the neck.
The largest methane ocean in Taurus is surrounded by estuaries that dig into the coast, almost scratching the large mesa mountains.
Taurus has a large portion of its surface covered in methane. This archipelago is one of the most accessible spots to one of the largest lakes.

trans-unit.source: The Fizzlebottom family is well known for their wealth. Algernon has decided to invest heavily in New Space, throwing money at startups to see how far they get. Your mission is to achieve some of the milestones he's set to unlock new technologies.

Buck Marshall is the mayor of Juno Village, a small settlement in Droo's largest mountain range. He's been trying to promote the region's aerospace sector, and finally someone gets to use the infrastructure he built, so prepare for some challenges.

General Schafer runs the not-so-secret Ali Base, a facility hidden in a salt lake surrounded by mountains. He'll send you some really interesting contracts, but he seems to be hiding something from you.
Evelyn is the director of the Droo Space Center. She'll assign you some of the hardest missions, but rest assured they come with good pay.
Wacky scientist though he is, Pricklespac is one of the most renowned researchers on Droo. He's looking for help gathering data to prove other forms of life exist in the Juno System.

trans-unit.source: Who wants to explore when you can farm the same contract over and over? Let's see how many contracts you can get.
Money doesn't grow from trees, you need to complete contracts from time to time to get some.
Can you get on track and complete a handful of contracts?
If you try to grow a company, the more contracts you fulfill the better you'll make, 15 is a pretty decent start.
You are farming those contracts like a champ, what are you doing to need that much cash?
At this point you have earned a good reputation, can you get into the triple digits?
Let the money flow, this will account for all your expenses.
The expenses pile up, by the time you realize you are burning millions as if they were paper.
Right now it may seem surreal to even think you will be expending so much… just wait.
If you manage to spend this much money, you may need to go get some fresh air.
Ok, this will actually be challenging, either you are playing a lot or you are making things out of gold if you hit this.
A trillion in expenses is what you would expect from a company going all around a stellar system, what are you even doing?
Launch unique crafts into the world.
The more you launch, the more experienced you get. Get familiar with the process.
You seem to be getting familiar with the dynamics, keep on going!
So far you have launched a handful of times, now things get real.
You must be getting the hang of this by now, what is sure is you are at least trying.
At this point are you even flying them or just launching and recovering a cheap craft to get this milestone?
Recover crafts to get money in return.
If you plan ahead, or just get lucky recovering your crafts, your savings will cover a large cut of your future investments.
Saving $100k in recoveries is really impressive, this is more than what your first crafts cost!
Imagine being a millionaire just from the money saved by recovering your crafts.
Many companies fail to understand the importance of recovery and refurbishment. By saving 10M$ you are going to have more saved money than their yearly incomes.
Saving a billion just from intelligent planning and engineering, this will put you in everyone's mouths.
Blow things up, each explosion will add one to the count.
There's no success without failure, and there's no fun without some explosions. Causing 10 explosions is just the start.
Aerospace is infamous for how easily things go South, but by the time you cause 50 explosions you'll start to get some looks.
If you get past 250 explosions either you are purposely blowing stuff up or you should reconsider your design process.
You are going for 1000 explosions!? How are you even getting this many?
You have to be doing something insanely well to earn enough money to blow up this much stuff, so now that you're at it, let's get those fireworks going!
How high you have gone. When in orbit, this is defined by your apoapsis.
Higher than the tallest of mountains, your first step towards reaching the stars.
Above 30km the atmosphere is thin enough for wings to be useless and drag low enough for hitting record speeds.
At 80km there is no air anymore, you have reached space!
To reach 300km you need a beefy rocket, no matter if you go straight up or orbit the planet.
You have reached far around Droo, it's time to reach the stars.
20km/s is a really fast speed, only for those who dare to get in orbit of Juno.
These are the speeds you would expect to see on a craft exploring the entirety of the Juno system, is it you?
These are insane speeds, you must be almost touching Juno's corona.
1% the speed of light, at this point you are pushing the game to its knees.
Do you have what it takes to go faster than light? The game sure doesn't, what are you even doing?
Try to dock as many unique crafts together as you can.
One of the most challenging things you can do in Droo orbit is docking, can you do it at least once?
If you want to start colonizing other worlds you need to get some experience docking things together.
Space Stations are usually built in orbit, they require lots of docks, can you pull it off?
You seem to be an expert at docking stuff together, a true professional space pilot!
At this point you should already know you don't need to be in orbit for the docks to count, right?
Put your droods on a stable orbit for their first time.
Droods are one of the most important assets you can have, are you going to risk losing them?
Sending a single drood to space is impressive, but by the time you have sent 3 nobody will have a doubt on your skills.
The best tool you have to explore space is your crew, train at least 10 in the absence of gravity.
Space Tourism, running a Space Station… you name it. You need to bring more droods up there.
For droods to become interplanetary you need to bring more and more to space, let's spread!

trans-unit.source: The map view is a great tool used to check your crafts from space, also being able to check other planets and moons in advance.
Knowing your rocket trajectory is vital for space travel, this will let you predict where and when you are going to be in a certain spot.
Complex space missions require advanced planning tools. Maneuver nodes will let you easily plan your burns to change your orbit according to plan.
The management of multiple crafts in orbit is complex, this is limited to ensure you don't pollute the system for no reason.
Dealing with clients can be overwhelming, but the more contracts you get, the more freedom in your selection you will have.
Regrets have never been less of a thing, quicksaving lets you set checkpoints during a mission and go back to them at any point.
Time traveling is a powerful tool, get a second chance after messing it up or hop into the designer to tweak the craft before coming back.
A menu with a handful set of tools that aren't officially supported but that can unlock loads of fun.
Is there a place you really like? Are you tired of having to get to orbit every time? Just save a launch location and done.
A menu with a handful set of tools that will let you teleport, change gravity, have infinite fuel… your wishes come true!
A context menu letting you set contracts as completed and access contract dev QoL tools.
Tired of being told you can't launch? No wonder! Do whatever you want with this unlocked.
Fuel lines let you send fuel across any part of your rocket, letting it reach your engines no matter what the configuration of the structure is.
Heatshield coatings give parts some extra protection to heat, peeling off the extra heat and thus running out over time.
The maximum size of the beacons.
The maximum size of a crew capsule.
The maximum size of a side detacher.
The maximum size of a docking port.
The maximum size of an electric motor.
The maximum size of an ion engine.
The maximum size of a jet engine.
The maximum size of a joint rotator.
The maximum size of a landing gear.
The maximum size of a landing gear.
The maximum size of the lights.
The maximum size of a parachute.
The maximum size of a piston.
The maximum size of a propeller assembly.
The maximum size of a RCS.
The maximum size of a rocket engine.
The maximum size of a shock.
The maximum size of a solar panel Array.
The maximum size of a rover wheel.
How large your chute can be, increasing its drag.
The length of a parachute chord can make it more stable.
The amount of volume in a command disc dedicated to store batteries.
The amount of volume in a command disc dedicated to store gyroscopes. These can point a craft but can be slow and expensive.
The amount of volume available for each crew member in a compartment.
Night Vision cameras allow you to see in the dark without the need of having lights, but they need at least some light to work.
Lead pellets you can put in your fuel tanks to adjust the CoM.
The pinch tool allows you to deform a fuselage to make it narrower on one side.
The slant tool lets you make a diagonal cut to the top face of a fuselage.
The clamp tool lets you cut sections out of a fuselage.
The curve tool lets you change the profile of a nosecone to any curve.
The amount of panels per row the array can have.
The amount of rows of panels the array can have.
How much the panel can be stretched to tweak its shape.
The brake torque affects how hard it can stop.
How fast the electric motor can spin given enough torque.
The torque of a motor defines how much force it can do.
The number of unique blades in the propeller assembly.
A set of hinges in the propeller blades, allowing for a variable pitch to fine tune their AoA.
The brake torque affects how hard it can stop a wheel.
Shock absorbers integrated in the wheels can help drive on bumpy terrain.
The torque of a motor defines how much force it can do.
The ability to retract the landing gear to reduce its drag footprint.
The amount of control surfaces you can pack in a single wing.
The wing chord is the size the wing can have between its front and back.
The wing span is its length, the distance between the root and the tip.
How thick a wing can get, making them more resistant to snaps and increasing its fuel storage capacity.
A solid propellant grain that results in a basic ramp up, hold, ramp down thrust curve.
A solid propellant with a hole in the center, resulting in a ramping up thrust curve.
A solid propellant grain that results in a ramping down thrust curve.
A solid propellant grain designed to produce a constant thrust over its entire burn.
A solid propellant grain that burns all the fuel at the start, resulting in a large impulse followed by a long residual thrust.
Bell shaped nozzles provide better performance than their conical counterparts. This one is resizable.
Cone shaped nozzles are about as basic as a nozzle can be, but this one is resizable.
It's a basic bell shaped rocket nozzle. More efficient than a cone.
Resizable bell shaped nozzle with more visual detail.
Advanced rocket nozzle with integrated cooling system.
Gigantic nozzle that pairs well with the Gas Generator II power cycle.
A milled piece of graphite, the simplest possible plug to put at the end of a rocket.
Large nozzle made for solid rocket boosters.
A gimbaled version of the Echo nozzle.
Aerospike nozzles offer better performance across a wide range of altitudes than bell or cone nozzles.
Gas generator is a powerful type of fuel injection capable of respectable chamber pressures.
It's the muscle car equivalent for rocket engines. It's powerful, but it's not too efficient.
Very advanced power cycle capable of extremely high chamber pressures.
The holy grail of power cycles capable of the highest chamber pressures at the highest efficiency.
The simplest possible rocket engine, it isn't very powerful but it works great in space. As a plus, it can gimbal, enabling for precise maneuvers.
A high tech rocket engine without a turbopump, using electric pumps to get the fuel into the chamber.
A solid rocket motor mounted on a sturdy gimbal capable of handling the high stress, enabling thrust vectoring for precise control.
A very small engine with very low efficiencies, perfect for hobbyists or stage separations.
An oversized version of the model rocket, perfect to increase the launch thrust of your rockets without spending too much.
Very efficient, but it doesn't pack a punch.
This can greatly increase fuel efficiency. All the cool engineers are doing it these days.
Increasing compression can increase fuel efficiency (and thrust up to a point), but also increases the length and weight of the core.
Reverse thrust lets you invert the force of the engine to help you brake the craft.
Afterburners can greatly increase thrust by lowering efficiency. And they look cool so win-win.
The addition of liquid oxygen allows the jet engine to run in absence of an atmosphere.
A chemical storage for your power needs, so you don't depend strictly on power generation.
Plane juice, your everyday kerosene, ready to be pumped into a jet engine to spin it up.
A more refined version of the jet fuel mixed with liquid oxygen, providing high energy density.
A very efficient fuel with an incredibly low density, requiring large tanks, mixed with liquid oxygen.
A light and efficient fuel right in between hydrolox and kerolox, mixed with liquid oxygen.
Pure hydrogen without any oxidizer, necessary for combustionless nuclear engines.
Purified tap water, useful not only as ballast but also for the combustionless nuclear engines.
Nasty hypergolic propellant, easy to ignite but insanely toxic.
A solid paste easy to store and cheap to produce, that once ignited can't be turned off.
A fuel tightly packed on the back of the Drood's suit, allowing for movement in space.
A noble gas with very heavy molecules, that once accelerated to high speeds can result in high efficiencies.
The max amount of Droods that can be hired in the current sandbox.
The more complex you need to make your crafts, the more stages you will need to manage part activations.
Low efficiency but cheap panels, good enough to power your most basic needs.
An old but reliable technology, more expensive than thin film but at the same time, more efficient.
Top tier solar panels, breaking the theoretical limits of maximum efficiency using fancy new materials.
Low efficiency but cheap panels, good enough to power your most basic needs.
An old but reliable technology, more expensive than thin film but at the same time, more efficient.
Top tier solar panels, breaking the theoretical limits of maximum efficiency using fancy new materials.
You will get new contracts after unlocking this tech.
You will get new contracts after unlocking this tech if you already have 'Check Your Staging'.
You will get new contracts after unlocking this tech, but they may require other dependencies like certain contracts being completed.
A budget ion propellant. A touch less efficient than xenon, but you can scoop it from the air.
Liquefied methane, the fuel half of methalox. Easy to harvest or brew up for a refuel far from home.
A storable monopropellant made from plain water. Gentler than hydrazine, but you can produce it just about anywhere.
Liquid oxygen on its own, the oxidizer half of every bipropellant. Scoopable from any atmosphere that carries it.
Highly refined kerosene, the fuel half of kerolox. Cheap, dense and easy to handle.
Just another aerospike but we had to cut some corners, it isn't as efficient but it is a tad lighter.
A variant of the cargo bay with no doors, for whatever you may need to have just half a fuselage.
Simpler and more rugged, this style of interstage will just ensure things don't come apart until you want.
A rocket chair to keep your crew comfy when under the high Gs of a launch.
A chair. Usable furniture. Ideal to sit down for a while and… yeah. A chair.
Striped variants of all the fuselages, including fuel tanks, interstages, fairings… To add a pop of color to your crafts.
Jet engines are expensive components, this cover will sure make things look more professional.
If you want to get fancy, chevron is the way to go, you will be cutting the air like butter.
A naked engine will afford you some mass, but leave the fragile components exposed to the elements.
You may try to lie to yourself thinking you want curved fans to get a better airflow, but we all know you just want their fancy looks.
As you get further away from the rotation axis the ideal angle of attack of the fan blades changes, this fan will match the ideal angle to result in the best looking engines.
A bunch of planks spinning fast. It does the job, but it sure is ugly.
The basic engine nozzle is boring, but effective, and for a cheap craft they will sure do the job.
Civilian nozzles are a fancier version of the basic, ideal for a wide range of sizes, from a small private one to a commercial passenger plane.
Who doesn't want to have a moving nozzle that adjusts its opening to maximize performance and allows for the hottests of exhausts?
A double wheel, allowing for twice the traction and braking power.
A single wheel attached on one of its ends.
A single wheel attached on both ends.
A curved door that will better match rounded fuselages.
Without a bay the landing gear will be left exposed once retracted.
A flat door… yeah, that is all, it is flat and it is a door.
A hinge that opens a pair of doors alongside the direction of the bay.
Just a hole, in case you hate aerodynamics.
A hinge that opens a door towards one side of the bay.
A hinge that opens a pair of doors towards the sides of the bay.
Although their colliders are still pointy, rounded noses are perfect for anything spherical.
An aerodynamic package meant to be mounted at the front of a craft to split the airstream.
A compact package ideal to just snap on the side of your craft to get a handy parachute.
A checkered pattern meant to make small parachutes easy to spot in the sky.
A ringed parachute. It makes for a perfect target if you want to train your aim.
A striped parachute similar to the ones used in crewed capsules.
A small boat propeller, perfect for motorboats of small submarines.
A very large boat propeller made out of heavy steel. Watch out for the icebergs.
A classic small aircraft propeller made out of aluminium. All rounded performance for a decent price.
A set of very agressive blades made out of composite materials, making them very light and powerful.
Let it fool you. It looks like a helicopter but it lacks the swashplate. Players will surely find a way to make helis out of this.
A curved blade capable of cutting through the air like a sword. Careful not to put your finger in it.
Carved out of wood to imitate the blades in the XX century fighters, perfect for replica lovers.
A rim containing a motor with normal torque and gear reduction.
A rim containing a motor with low torque and a huge gear reduction to get good torque using less power, also keeping speeds down.
A rim containing a motor designed for speed, with decent torque and a great gear increment allowing for very high speeds.
A rim containing a cheap motor with low torque and a normal gear reduction.
A rim containing a motor with tons of torque and a good gear reduction to further increase it.
A well balanced wheel with normal grip on any surface.
A tire with insanely good offroad grip but very dense and expensive.
A tire with great grip when offroad but mediocre over concrete.
The perfect tire for races, with very good grip on concrete but terrible when offroading.
An average tire with decent grip on concrete and mediocre grip offroad.
What Are You Even Trying To Do

trans-unit.note: Fits 429px at 20px. Contracts/*.xml: contract name + subtitle + flair + description (long/short). Keys auto-derived from contract id. Default and Hybrid Contracts/*.xml share these keys (Hybrid differs only in tiny typo edits). Per-completion-count variants use Completions<N>.{Long,Short}

trans-unit.source: Go higher than 25km and drop nearby.

Once you send your fireworks high enough, hitting a house in the village becomes a huge problem, but going too far makes finding the scraps annoying. Try to crash no farther than 20km, but no closer than 500m from the launchpad.
Leave the atmosphere with a payload.
Droo's atmosphere ends right under 80km, can you go to space to expose a probe a scientist has sent me?
Fireworks are one of the best inventions of droomankind. Fly high, blow up.
Drop a rocket far from the village.
Before hoping to reach space, you need some horizontal speed, since orbit requires going sideways more than up. Try to fall @Distance:distance away from the village.
Blow up to entertain the neighbors.

Everyone loves explosions, especially far from your property. Create a fireworks spectacle by blowing something up with enough kick at high altitude. You can find a fuel tank's explosive power in the Design Info panel in the designer.
Drop a rocket in the water.
Polluting the oceans is bad, but neighbors complaining about things dropping on their lands is worse. Launch a rocket and drop it in any ocean.
The scientist who gave me the probe you sent to space has some things for you to do, but he first wants to be sure you can reach orbit. Can you give it a go?
One advantage of a huge ramp on the edge of a cliff is you can fly without much effort. Go airborne for more than @Distance:distance after jumping off the end of the runway.
You've already tried to jump as far as possible from the runway; now you have to take off from it. You can be wise and get some wings, or yolo it and find an alternative. You do you.
Visit some locations in the Juno Village.
I want to be sure you know how to move around properly without blowing up (too much). Visit these 4 spots in any order. Once done, come to the Town Hall.
Go up the peak near the village.

The peak right next to our village has some of the best views I've seen. Can you go up there to enjoy them and take a couple photos? If your craft slides too much, increase its torque by maxing out the Gear Ratio.
To bring some tourists to the village we're preparing some hiking routes. Can you help us scout them to see if they're viable?
Follow the route up the mountain.

I've been watching videos lately and extreme sports seem trendy. To see if we can attract some sporty tourists, can you climb the mountain next to the village? It's tough, but we have a route planned to the top.
Bring some supplies to the camp.

We need supplies brought to the camp on the mountain top. Drive or fly them, we don't care, just get them there. Careful not to bump the tents; these days they make them rock solid.

You can place these packages on your craft but they won't stick to it, so you'll have to figure out how to keep them from falling while still being able to leave them at the target. You can identify these non-sticky parts by their white attachpoints.
Achieve an air-speed record without going too high.
The Wright Brothers were the first to fly at a whopping… 3m/s. You can do better, can't you?
To get airborne you need to catch some airspeed. The Mach number represents the speed of sound at a given altitude, and around the Village a Mach number of 0.25 is just under 100 m/s.
Going supersonic is cool, but you have to aim for realistic goals. Can you first get to Mach 0.5?
They call Mach 1 the sound barrier, but is it a barrier for you?
Going supersonic is fun, but where the real challenge starts is when you reach hypersonic speeds.
Mountain villages aren't known for how fast you can drive past them, reaching 50km/h would be insane!
100km/h or 60mph has been always the reference speed for acceleration tests, can you even beat it?
By the time you are offroading at 200km/h you know you are into something… be aware of the bumps!
Rapid and Raging (TM). This is already in the land of super-cars, do you have the drip?
It's time to dip your toes in the water. Find the closest pond, lake or ocean and try to see if you float.
Reaching 65 knots is something only reserved for the best interceptors, will they catch you?
You are an experienced sailor it seems, but drag hits hard underwater, go faster than 50 m/s.
If you haven't sunk yet, going at 70m/s shouldn't be that hard.
It's time to gather some dust on those wheels. Make a car and drive it for @DistanceTarget:distance.
Endurance is important if you want to show everyone you are both a great engineer and a skilled pilot. Go for a @DistanceTarget:distance drive.
Are you ready to go for a trip? I want to see if you are capable of driving around for @DistanceTarget:distance without falling asleep.
Once you leave the atmosphere and you free yourself from its drag, there's nothing stopping you from going as fast as you want.
Going at 2000 m/s doesn't sound impressive, until you realize that is 7200 km/h. That's some speed.
Reaching a LEO orbit means going really fast. The higher you go, the slower the speed, but the harder it is to get there. For a low orbit, you'll need to go faster than 3000 m/s.
In order to get to the moons or even reach other planets, you will need some insane speeds.
Go through all the checkpoints in any order.
This is a time trial, so get your boots tight! Go through all the checkpoints in any order before time runs out. The timer starts once you pass through any checkpoint.
Go through all the checkpoints in any order.
This is a time trial, so get your boots tight! Go through all the checkpoints in any order before the time runs out.
I saw you gained access to the Ali Base recently, let's have some fun. This is a time trial, so get your boots tight!
Go through all the checkpoints in any order.
After watching you race in Ali, I noticed they have a really interesting wall all around the base. How fast can you ride it?
Go through all the checkpoints in any order.
This is a time trial, so get your boots tight! Go through all the checkpoints in any order before the time runs out.
It seems like only yesterday you were launching from the village… Now we have even better taxiways! This is a time trial, so get your boots tight!
Go through all the checkpoints in any order.
This is a time trial, so get your boots tight! Go through all the checkpoints in any order before the time runs out.
Go through all the checkpoints in any order.
This is a time trial, so get your boots tight! Go through all the checkpoints in any order before the time runs out.
Go through all the checkpoints in order.
This is a time trial for planes, so get your gloves tight! Go through all the checkpoints in order before the time runs out.
Go through all the checkpoints in order.
This is a time trial for planes, so get your gloves tight! Go through all the checkpoints in order before the time runs out.
Go through all the checkpoints in order.
This is a time trial for planes, so get your gloves tight! Go through all the checkpoints in order before the time runs out.
Go through all the checkpoints in order.

I saw some interesting hangars and overhangs around the DSC. Can you thread the needle? This is a time trial for planes, so get your gloves tight! Hit all the checkpoints in order before time runs out.
While attempting an air race near Juno Village, a Drood crashed their SimpleCub! Can you safely bring them back to the Juno Village? Time is critical!
A pair of reckless Droods pushed a SimpleOffroad to its limits and a little beyond that. Can you bring them back safely to the Juno Village?
Fly low around the desert base.

Our systems detected you flying around the planet, and you seem like the perfect candidate for one of our missions. We're validating the new ALI Base radars: fly 10km under 150m above the ground at mach 1 or above near the base.
We've been closely following your launch activity and you seem to be doing pretty well. Our needs are a bit special, though: we need you to prove you can work with us by getting to orbit fast.
Bring some crates to the outpost.
We need to bring a couple of crates full of PETN to the desert base outpost. They're very delicate, so be careful with them — we don't need stunts for this one.
Bring some supplies to the Outpost.
We need to bring some supplies to the Outpost, we don't care if you drive or fly them as long as they get there.
Bring some supplies to the Launchpad.
We need to bring some supplies to the Ali Launchpad, we don't care if you drive or fly them as long as they get there.
Algernon's private jet made an emergency landing on rough terrain. Luckily he wasn't aboard, just his crew. Bring them back to the Ali Outpost quickly, no time to waste.
Somehow a Drood broke their motorboat and is stranded at sea. They've asked me for help, but I'm sure you're skilled enough to handle the situation yourself.
Pricklespac sent a team of Droods to the pole, but their Polar Exploration Vehicle fell into a crevasse and is inoperable. Bring them back to the Ali Base before they freeze.
Shotwell has called for help with a SimpleRCV that is stuck in the middle of nowhere. Can you safely transport them to the DSC Port?
Yet another one of those cheap SimpleCrews still using 100% sized docking ports is leaking again. This time it was crewed, though. Can you figure out how to bring the Drood back?

Algernon sent a couple of Droods on a space trip aboard his flashy Rapture capsule and now they're stuck in space. He won't rescue them, so it's your job now. They have a 200% size docking port — figure it out.

A crew of 3 is stuck in an experimental shuttle we launched a couple weeks ago into a polar orbit for some research I needed. It has a 400% size docking port; if you can figure out how, you can try to ride it back.
Shotwell needs help bringing back a Drood stranded in orbit of Luna, in a Bruno Capsule with a 100% size docking port. Don't mess this one up or it'll be terrible PR.
2 Droods in a LM Ascent Stage

Somehow Shotwell sent another mission to Luna, and it got stranded again. This time it's the Ascent Stage of their Luna Module, so it's on a really low orbit. It has a 100% size docking port; bring them back without crashing them into Luna.

I have unsurprising news for you. Shotwell has lost yet another craft orbiting Luna, this time a flashy new Nebula Capsule with a 200% size docking port. It's on a really extreme orbit, good luck approaching it.
Yet another Luna Module has malfunctioned, this time on the surface of Luna, and is inoperable. Try to bring those Droods back home.
The LunaTown Base got one of its windows punctured somehow, you need to get there really quick to rescue the two Droods that survived the event.

Another of Algernon's toys has failed, this time the electrical system in a Lunar Lander. Now the crew can't launch and their elevator won't work, so figure out a way to get them down to the surface and then back home.
We have detected some potentially dangerous debris in orbit. You must eliminate it asap.
Get a payload to the DSC port.
If you show you can get your crafts to the water safely, we'll let you use our port in the future. This will make water recovery substantially cheaper.
Land a craft safely in the village.

Our space center runways are a valuable asset we can't afford to lose, so first we need to ensure you can land safely in a rough situation. Build a crewed craft capable of Mach 3, then land it safely on the runway at the village.
Bring a large payload to the Hippolyta GS.

We're looking for someone who can carry a very large payload all the way down to the Hippolyta Ground Station. The Station has no runway, so we can't ship it ourselves. Pull this off and we'll let you use our best runway at the DSC.
Land a booster on the Drone Ship.
Before you can launch from our best launchpad, we need to verify you know what you're doing. Get on a suborbital trajectory and then land on the barge to unlock the raised launchpad.
Get a large payload to space.
We want to see if you can put a @Mass:mass craft into orbit. If you can, we'll let you use our large launchpad. It's just a patch of concrete, but it'll let you launch really huge things.
Get a rover to Luna to drive around the South Pole base.

Before you can use our infrastructure at Luna, we need to check you can actually get there yourself and survive the environment. So, get a rover to the base and drive until you exit the crater, without flying there.
Bring a probe around the system and out.

After blowing our whole budget building the infrastructure on Luna, we're running short. I need something really impressive so we can ask for more funds.

We have a Traveler Probe ready: bring it to at least 3 of Droo's planets, then get it out of Juno's Sphere of Influence.

We need your help building the Space Port Esperanza (SPE) in Low Droo Orbit. First, bring up the Radix Module. This is a key step in the DSC's efforts to colonize the Juno System, so get it right and many contracts will follow.

We don't like leaving debris around Droo if we can avoid it. Make sure you safely deorbit your stage!

Now that Radix is in orbit, we want to start building up SPE. Dock the Expansion Module to the Radix Module; it brings needed resources and more docking capabilities, but you'll need to bring some monoprop yourself to maneuver it.

We don't like to leave debris around Droo if we can avoid it. Make sure you safely deorbit your stage!

Dock the Nexus Cross to the Space Port Esperanza. These docking hubs expand the SPE's docking capacity and will host future DSC Modules and even your own, but you'll need to bring some monoprop yourself to maneuver it.

We don't like leaving debris around Droo if we can help it. Make sure you safely deorbit your stage!

Dock the Habitation Module to the Space Port Esperanza. These modules create a comfortable, spacious place for inhabitants to reside, but you'll need to bring some monoprop yourself to maneuver it.

We don't like to leave debris around Droo if we can avoid it. Make sure you safely deorbit your stage!

Dock the Cupola Module to the Space Port Esperanza. It'll give crew and tourists inside excellent views of Droo, but you'll need to bring some monoprop yourself to maneuver it.

We don't like leaving debris around Droo if we can avoid it. Make sure you safely deorbit your stage!

Dock the Solar Array to the Space Port Esperanza. Once all the solar arrays are docked to the SPE, they'll provide enough power for all operations, but you'll need to bring some monoprop yourself to maneuver it.

We don't like to leave debris around Droo if we can avoid it. Make sure you safely deorbit your stage!

Dock the @Name to the Space Port Esperanza.

We don't like leaving debris around Droo if we can help it. Make sure you safely deorbit your stage!

Dock the Fuel Depot Core to the Space Port Esperanza. This core infrastructure lets us expand our resources aboard the SPE, including keeping fuel for any future missions that need a bit of extra gas.

We don't like to leave debris around Droo if we can avoid it. Make sure you safely deorbit your stage!

Dock the @Name Fuel Sphere to the Fuel Depot Core. These fueling spheres have unique docking interfaces, so make sure you dock to the Depot Core!

We don't like to leave debris around Droo if we can avoid it. Make sure you safely deorbit your stage!
Go through all the checkpoints in order.
Buck told me you're a great pilot. I've prepared a plane race to watch you zoom past my window and see if it's true. Get ready for a real challenge.
Bring some supplies to the camp.
Bring some supplies to my research station near the Juno Village. You can drive or fly, as long as you don't break anything.
Go through all the checkpoints in order.

Your delivery to the Research Station was impressive. I've been looking for help for a while and you seem like a perfect fit. To test that, I need you to visit a series of landmarks. Speed isn't important, just visit them all in order. It's a long drive over steep terrain, so consider flying point to point, or a hybrid approach.
Go to the indicated locations and inspect them.
I need to grab some samples from one of Droo's biomes. Go there and grab @Samples samples.
Drop a payload in the ocean.
I need to bring a submarine to the designated location to run some experiments, can you get it there?
Bring a container to one of the Ground Stations.
I need some tools and resources to keep the Ground Station running, but it's really far from the Research Station. Can you bring me a container?
Can you go to orbit? I need you to be close to a very specific orbit, can you make it there?
Carry a payload to the desired orbit.

I need help getting some satellites into orbit. Let's start easy: can you put this CubeSat into any orbit? I've added a deployer to ease integration, but you decide where it goes in the rocket. It can fit next to an engine, inside a fairing if you've unlocked them, or you can even eject the nosecone with an interstage holding the payload inside.
Carry a payload to the desired orbit.

I have @SatCount @SatName@SatCount:s ready for orbit, mind helping? I've already added the deployment gear to ease integration.

You can do more than one satellite contract at a time, I won't complain as long as they reach their destination. If you do, make sure you assign the @SatName@SatCount:s to the right contract in the designer.

Heliosynchronous orbits use orbital precession to keep the orbit's position relative to the sun throughout an entire year. This game's physics aren't that fancy, but it's a cool orbit regardless. Can you get something into such an odd orbit?
My satellites have detected weird activity on Droo's surface, can you bring a telescope to Droostationary orbit so I can observe what is going on?

I need you to fly by Luna to study its orbital conditions. My studies show these bodies' physics are governed by something called 'Spheres of Influence', a region of space where their gravity is stronger than any other nearby body's, so your orbits are only affected by it.
I need you to fly by @Moon to study its orbital conditions. You just need to get close enough to be in its Sphere of Influence.
I need you to orbit Brigo so we can start studying it in depth. Get into its sphere of influence and slow down enough to get captured.
I need you to get in orbit of @Moon, with an apoapsis lower than @Apoapsis:distance
Carry a payload to the desired orbit.
I have a @ProbeName Probe ready to be put into @Moon orbit, mind helping? I have already added the deployment gear to ease the integration.
I need you to reach the surface of @Moon to carry some experiments. The sensors aren't very sensitive, so no need to soft land it — though I've added an airbag just in case.

I need you to bring a set of more sensitive sensors to the surface of @Moon, so no bouncing this time.

I've prepared a lander with an engine and legs, but you need to bring it to @Moon orbit and drive it down to the surface — not that I didn't trust you to build it.

I appreciate your landing skills, but I need a bit more precision. I've made a rover, can you bring it to @Moon?

This time you'll have to make the lander, bring the Rover there, and drive it for me. Remember, you can select @Moon in the craft info panel in the designer to better tune your engine thrust, and legs will help soften the touchdown.
Can you get to @Moon and safely land? Your craft has to stay landed for at least 30 seconds.
I need you to fly by @Planet to study its orbital conditions. You just need to get close enough to be in its Sphere of Influence.
I need you to get in orbit of @Planet, with an apoapsis lower than @Apoapsis:distance
Can you get to @Planet and safely land? Your craft has to stay landed for at least 30 seconds.

We have @Count @Count:plural(tourist|tourists) who want to feel special and tell their friends they've been to space, but they don't want to be cramped in a tight container for too long.

Get them out of the atmosphere for a few minutes and return them safely, keeping things smooth.

Don't bring random tourists, they haven't paid! Grab them from the Payloads section, they'll be waiting there.
Time to fly! Are you ready?
%ActivateInstruction% to activate your first stage, igniting your engine. Since it's a solid engine, once ignited you won't be able to stop it or adjust its power.
Wait for your engine to ramp up
At the bottom of your screen you can find the main dashboard.

You can switch between AGL and ASL altitudes. AGL is your distance to the ground (or to the water above oceans); ASL is your distance to Sea Level, useful once you're high enough to ignore the terrain, since it better shows how close to space you are.
You can also switch between Surface and Orbit speeds. Surface accounts for the planet's rotation, while Orbit doesn't. Whenever you target another craft, a third mode shows your relative speed.

As you change modes, you'll see the green arrow in the nav sphere move around. It adapts to your velocity mode to show where forward is pointing. Again, with something targeted, it shows the direction of your relative speed.
Use the nav sphere to change your rocket's heading. This automatically uses the engine gimbals, wings, gyroscopes, and more to try to point the craft where you want.

A really useful tool for any pilot is the nav ball. This sphere of strikes and numbers shows where you're looking. Its two colored halves are split by the horizon line. If all's going well right now you shouldn't see it, since your craft is pointing up.
You also have a map to find where you are. You can zoom in and out and change its orientation. It can be really useful, especially early on before you've unlocked the more advanced map view.
Crash at least 500m away from the village.
Time to touch down! No need to survive this one.
Wait for your first stage to run out of fuel.
Now it's on you, wait until the rocket goes higher than 80km and then stage again to expose the probe.
Select a part to blow it up

You've reached the necessary altitude, now it's time to blow this thing up! Select a fuel tank by clicking it to show a menu with more details about the part and a nice orange button. That's where the boom begins.
Select your command disc and blow up the craft before it goes too low!
Crash at least @Distance:distance away from the village.
Time to touch down! No need to survive this one.
Make sure the explosion has more than @Explosion boom power in a single fuel tank.
Time to drop, fall in the water.
%ActivateInstruction% to activate your first stage. This will activate your engines.
Wait until the booster's fuel is depleted. Your next step will happen at around 6km AGL, so relax, but not too much.
%ActivateInstruction% to activate your second stage. Remember to throttle up this time, it's no longer a solid motor.
Your rocket will now start tilting. This is important because to be in orbit you need to go sideways very fast.
You can build your rocket to follow a natural gravity turn. This forces it to pitch down as it rises, following an efficient path to orbit without the need for complex guidance systems.
Wait until the fuel in this stage is depleted.
%ActivateInstruction% to activate your third stage. Third time is the charm.
Almost there, burn your engine until your Apoapsis passes 150km. The Apoapsis is the highest point in your trajectory.
You can speed up game time to reduce waiting. Wait until you're out of the atmosphere to increase game speed.
Your final maneuver can be performed more efficiently closer to your apoapsis, wait until you are just 10 seconds away from it.
At last, raise your periapsis, the lowest point in the orbit, until it's higher than the atmosphere. This way you won't touch it at any moment, keeping you in orbit.
You need to go faster than 3300 m/s to get to orbital speeds at this height, you are almost there!
Now that you have reached orbit you are going to be asked to get to precise orbits, let's see how that is done.
The easiest way to adjust an orbit is to wait until the craft reaches its highest or lowest point and change one thing at a time. To adjust the apoapsis, be at the periapsis, and vice versa.
Since your apoapsis went a tad too high, the orbit is very elliptical. Let's make it more circular by waiting until you're at periapsis to lower it.
Let's wait for the craft to be close to its periapsis.
Time to fly! Are you ready?
Controlling a vehicle's heading is very important. For cars it's typical to use either Yaw or Roll. This one uses Roll, but let's try both.
Controlling a vehicle's heading is very important. For cars it's typical to use either Yaw or Roll. This one uses Roll, but let's try both.
As expected Roll did nothing, now look at the front wheels while using Yaw.
As expected Roll did nothing, now look at the front wheels while using Yaw.
Sometimes you may find the input of the wheels set to the Throttle, but that doesn't let you reverse the car, let's use Pitch instead.
If you want to have finer control or to leave an input fixed at a defined value then you can use the input sliders.
Roll down to the end of the runway
Get at least @Distance:distance away before you touch the ground
Time to fly! Are you ready?
In the 'The Jump' tutorial we had you use pitch for the wheels, but now pitch controls the wings, so let's figure out the new controls.
Look at the wing while using the pitch and roll to see the control surfaces move.
The pitch inputs are inverted, pushing down will pitch up, pushing up will pitch down.
The pitch inputs are inverted, pushing down will pitch up, pushing up will pitch down.
The roll inputs let you tilt the plane to a side. This, combined with pitch will let you turn around.
The roll inputs let you tilt the plane to a side. This, combined with pitch will let you turn around.
Set your throttle to max to gather speed and try to keep it straight, since you won't have any source of propulsion after take-off.
Roll down to the end of the runway
Let's kill the wheels so they don't waste battery and engage the autopilot. The autopilot will try to keep you pointing in the desired direction.
Great job! Now it's time to have some fun before you lose your speed, let's do some loops!
Remember to bring at least a camera with you.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from EvaChair1.xml

trans-unit.source: Astronauts will stand as long as you ask them to, but sometimes it's nice to give them a break and let them sit down.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Fairing1.xml

trans-unit.source: Protects precious cargo on its way to space.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from FairingBase1.xml

trans-unit.source: The base of your fairings. When using fairings, this must be the first part you connect to your craft.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from FairingNoseCone1.xml

trans-unit.source: Nose cone specially designed to only connect to fairings.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Fin1.xml

trans-unit.source: Smaller wing section designed for rockets.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from FuelAdapter1.xml

trans-unit.source: Makes it easier to connect engines to odd places on fuel tanks.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Fuselage1.xml

trans-unit.source: Versatile fuel tank that can be resized into many shapes and can hold many different types of fuel.
A properly sized, handy fuel tank preset to hold battery, in case you don't feel like using the built-in battery of a command disc.
If you don't worry about weight and you don't feel like bringing some solar panels with you, this clearly over-sized battery will do.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Gauge1.xml
Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from GaugeBase1.xml
Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from GaugeBundle.xml
Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Generator1.xml

trans-unit.source: A generator that turns fuel into power. It's far from efficient at burning it, but can be a lighter, more compact alternative to large batteries.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Generator2.xml

trans-unit.source: Radioisotope Thermal Generators act as a passive power source thanks to their insanely radioactive plutonium core. With one you can have power anywhere in the system, but it doesn't come cheap.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Gyroscope1.xml

trans-unit.source: Allows attitude control without thrust. Uses electricity.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from HeatShield1.xml

trans-unit.source: Provides protection from intense heat during re-entry.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from HingeRotator1.xml

trans-unit.source: Small motor that can rotate parts around a hinge.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Inlet1.xml

trans-unit.source: Inlets suck in air for jet engines. Make sure the front of the inlet isn't blocked by other parts, because that can obstruct its airflow.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from IonEngine1.xml

trans-unit.source: Extremely low power, high-efficiency engine that expels ions at nearly 50km/s. Requires electricity.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from JetEngine1.xml

trans-unit.source: High-bypass jet engines are the most fuel efficient style of jet engines, and are more commonly found on passenger airplanes where money matters.
A low-bypass jet engine that trades fuel efficiency for more thrust. It also includes an afterburner, which significantly boosts thrust and makes it totally rad.
Indecisive about where to go? Fear no more! This jet engine blends the best of both worlds, feeding extra oxygen to its afterburner so it works even in space.
With a great balance between power and efficiency, mid-bypass turbofans are the perfect choice for mid size planes and small and fancy private jets.
Turbojets are the oldest and least efficient jet engines. These were designed before engineers knew that redirecting some air around the core was more fuel efficient and produced more thrust.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from KomodoBundle.xml

trans-unit.source: Command pod which includes a small amount of fuel, built-in engines, and a rotating nose cone.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Label1.xml

trans-unit.source: Displays text. For labeling stuff, or whatever.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from LandingGear1.xml
Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from LandingLeg1.xml

trans-unit.source: Useful for landing without smashing your engine into the ground.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from LandingLeg2.xml

trans-unit.source: A sturdy set of legs useful for landing without smashing your engines into the ground, with great aero for how far they can deploy

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from LandingLeg3.xml

trans-unit.source: A very advanced and modern landing leg that will allow you to bring down the rockets of the future

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from LandingLeg4.xml

trans-unit.source: A small and simple landing leg, capable of slowing down the impact on moon landers

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Light1.xml

trans-unit.source: Use these to help light your way.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Mfd1.xml

trans-unit.source: Runs special Vizzy programs to display interactive widgets during flight.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from NoseCone1.xml

trans-unit.source: When used correctly, nose cones can reduce drag.
Half a sphere. Two of these make a ball. Don't expect them to roll nice though, the collider is just a cone, sadly.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Package.xml
Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Parachute1.xml

trans-unit.source: With this you should hopefully touch down with a more gentle touch, but don't push them too far or they will break.
Activate these in an atmosphere to reduce your chances of rapid unplanned disassembly.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Piston1.xml

trans-unit.source: Push parts away from each other with a customizable hydraulic piston.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from PropellerAssembly1.xml

trans-unit.source: Your classic civilian small aircraft propeller, suited for the early crafts that require well rounded performance for cheap.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from PropellerBundles.xml

trans-unit.source: Your classic civilian small aircraft propeller, suited for the early crafts that require well rounded performance for cheap.
A large propeller perfect for large aircraft, a couple of these will provide the thrust you need to get things going.
A set of powerful lightweight blades perfect for vertical take-off and landing.
Modern and efficient blades ideal for long-range flight, just make sure you keep your fingers away from it.
A small boat propeller. The Oceans are yours now! Well, more like lakes, but you get the point.
A large boat propeller for long-range trips and huge ships, made of heavy steel, so get ahold of a beefy motor for it.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from RCSNozzle1.xml

trans-unit.source: Reaction control nozzles help provide precise attitude control. Uses monopropellant.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from RCSNozzle2.xml

trans-unit.source: A reaction control nozzle that gimbals for far greater control than a standard RCS nozzle. Some say it can do the work of five normal RCS nozzles.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from RocketEngine1.xml

trans-unit.source: This engine is not about power, but about precision. Capable of small orbit and attitude adjustments, this engine is a must in any deep space mission.
As close as a deflating balloon you can get in terms of complexity, but also in terms of thrust.
Low-power engine useful for second stages and landing on small bodies. Its electric pump allows a quick start and very low throttling, but requires some batteries on board.
Highly efficient nuclear thermal engine. Warning: Do not lick.
Powerful engine that can be used for takeoff and orbiting. Not a great choice for landing on moons.
A sophisticated methalox engine with great efficiency thanks to one of the most advanced pump systems ever seen.
Powerful and efficient engine that uses hydrolox and staged combustion.
It's heavy, expensive, and drinks RP-1 like there's no tomorrow, but it will have the power to get even your most poorly engineered contraptions into space.
Sugar, spice and everything nice. The favorite toy of any rocket nerd.
Powerful and cheap, but inefficient. Cannot be shut down once ignited.
An extremely powerful solid rocket motor. Brute forces its usefulness through sheer power with no concern for efficiency whatsoever.
An extremely powerful solid rocket motor with a gimbal. This beast can flex its muscles when necessary.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from RotatingNoseCone1.xml
Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Rotator1.xml

trans-unit.source: Small motor that can rotate parts.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from RoverWheel1.xml

trans-unit.source: Resizable wheels that have a built-in electric motor.
Resizable wheels that have a built-in electric motor.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Shock1.xml

trans-unit.source: Shocks are useful when you want to soften impact with terra firma.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from SolarPanel1.xml

trans-unit.source: Single, stationary solar panel that can be resized.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from SolarPanelArray.xml

trans-unit.source: Configurable solar panel array that stows away into a remarkably small space.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from StructuralPanel1.xml

trans-unit.source: It may look like a wing, but it has no wing physics simulation. Great when you need lots of wing-like shapes but don't care if they generate lift. They use less processing power than a normal wing, so your design runs a little faster.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Strut1.xml

trans-unit.source: Resizable strut that can help bolster your crafts.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from TestPilot.xml

trans-unit.source: Human like device that can be used to monitor the safety of your crafts.

trans-unit.note: Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from ToggleSwitch1.xml
Fits 237px at 16px. DesignerPart presets from Wing1.xml

trans-unit.source: Large wing section designed with airplanes in mind.

Please send us your thoughts about this contract. Thanks!
Click this to recenter your camera.

Argon for ion engines, a cheaper stand-in for xenon at the cost of slightly lower efficiency. Where an atmosphere carries it at all it tends to be sparse, so gathering a useful amount takes a dedicated scoop and some patience.
Battery is used to power many components of a craft, and unlike fuel, it can be regenerated.

Methane for use as the fuel component in Methalox rocket engines. It turns up as atmospheric gas, surface ice, and even liquid lakes, so a harvester can often top up in the field. Store alongside an Oxygen tank and the engine will burn them together when the combined Methalox mixture tank is depleted.

Carbon dioxide, harvested from the atmosphere where a world has one or mined from frozen surface deposits. On its own it's just cargo, but feed it to a Sabatier converter with some hydrogen and it becomes methane fuel.
Now that's what I call high-quality H2O.

A storable monopropellant that runs without a separate oxidizer, handy for RCS and small thrusters. It's less efficient than hydrazine, but you can make it from nothing but water, so it's the easy choice for a self-sufficient base.
Special kerosene for use in jet engines. Note: Jet engines don't need to be directly connected to fuel tanks with jet fuel. As long as your craft has some, they will work.
It's for jetpacks…also this shouldn't be showing up anywhere.

Hydrogen for use in rocket engines. Without an oxidizer it is even more efficient, but can then only be used in nuclear rocket engines. Also serves as the fuel component for Hydrolox engines when stored alongside Oxygen tanks, and a scoop can harvest it from any atmosphere rich enough in it.

Oxygen for use as the oxidizer component in bipropellant rocket engines. Cryogenic in storage, but a scoop can pull it straight from an atmosphere that carries it. Store alongside a compatible fuel (Kerosene, Hydrogen, or Methane) and the engine will burn them together when the combined mixture tank is depleted.
Oxygen and methane for use in rocket engines. Somewhat more efficient than kerolox, but easier to work with than hydrolox.
Oxygen and hydrogen for use in rocket engines. Hydrolox is very efficient, but it has extremely low density and therefore requires larger fuel tanks.
Oxygen and kerosene for use in rocket engines. It's cheap and only moderately cryogenic so it's safer and easier to work with. The downside is that it's not as efficient as some of the other fuels.
Toxic? Maybe. But its flexibility is perfect for RCS and simple engines. If you smell ammonia, run.
Nitrogen, scooped from the atmosphere of any world that has one. Nothing burns it directly, but combine it with hydrogen in a converter and you can synthesize hydrazine, a potent storable propellant.
Only for those who dare to play with fire, watch for your fingers.

Highly refined kerosene (RP-1) for use as the fuel component in Kerolox rocket engines. Store alongside an Oxygen tank and the engine will burn them together when the combined Kerolox mixture tank is depleted.
Loose surface rock and dust, drilled straight from the ground. No engine burns it and no converter processes it, but with a drill and a tank you can haul it back from anywhere you can land.
Solid fuel for use in rocket engines. It packs a lot of impulse into a small space, but it is heavy and expensive.
Xenon is used by ion engines. It's an inert gas, so it won't cause huge explosions. Depending on what you're going for that might be a good thing or a bad thing.
Gradients in Unity do not support more than 8 {0} keys.
You have passed this requirement (for now)
Build a rocket that can reach an altitude of 100km above sea level.
I can show you how to build a rocket. It'll take only about 10 minutes, but the knowledge will last a lifetime! It'll be fun!

Practice docking with a satellite. Just ease forward and give the satellite a little kiss with your docking port. Once at close range, the docking port applies a small magnetic force to help align the two ports together.

The European Space Agency is visiting Jupiter for the first time with the JUpiter ICy moons Explorer.
To commemorate this, can you bring JUICE to Tydos? Fuel is low, so you may need some Gravity Assists. Keep your deltaV usage as low as possible!
Launch from Droo and reach escape velocity so your orbit becomes hyperbolic. The level ends once you leave Droo's Sphere of Influence (SOI). You must use less than 60kL of fuel to win.
I can show you how to fly the rocket from the Designer Tutorial. All the way from blast-off to orbit.
Practice landing on Luna. It's not an easy thing to do, so this is a great place to learn some technique.

Fly your rocket as far as you can without going above 5,000 meters or touching the ground. You must fly more than 50km to pass. Don't worry about landing safely; just go far and do a spectacular crash landing.
Get into a low orbit around Droo. Your periapsis must be at least 100km and you must use less than 10kL of fuel.

How fast can you go? You have 20 days to reach the maximum speed possible. Exceed 30,000m/s to win. Speed is calculated relative to the body you're orbiting.
Tip: Sometimes you have to slow down to speed up! Also, if you're using more than 25-30 engines, you're not doing it right!
Build a rocket that exceeds 750m/s before reaching 2km above ground level. You must fly straight up. Drift sideways more than 100 meters and you fail this challenge.
Get into medium orbit around Droo. At least 5,000km periapsis. You must use less than 200 kL of fuel.

Land on Luna using as little fuel as possible. Apollo 11 did this back in 1969 with an on-board computer less powerful than your phone, so this should be easy, right?
You must use less than 50kL of fuel to win.
I hope you like a challenge. Blast off from Droo, make your way to Luna, and reach a stable orbit around it using less than 50kL of fuel. Your Periapsis must be at least 25km for the orbit to count.
Get to Luna as fast as you can. Don't worry about landing. The timer stops whenever you smash into Luna's surface. You have 10 hours to accomplish your mission. Good luck!

You're given a small rocket with very little fuel and must fly it as far as you can. You must travel at least 15km to win.
Tip: Atmospheric drag can really slow you down, but it decreases quickly as you gain altitude.

Starting in orbit around Droo with a small rocket, you must make your way back to Droo and parachute safely to the ground.
Do a retrograde burn to bring your orbit into the atmosphere, then land safely.
Beware of part damage from excessive heat during re-entry.
Get into orbit around Droo. Your periapsis must be at least 250km and your inclination between 85 and 95 degrees. You must use less than 50 kL of fuel.
Build a rocket, launch from Droo, and rendezvous with the satellite already in orbit. This is an extremely challenging endeavor, far harder than Luna Landing.
You need a docking port to dock with the satellite!

Our shuttle was coming in for a landing when we remembered we don't know how to pilot a space shuttle…
Would you please lend us a hand?
See how quickly you can orbit Droo. Your Periapsis must be at least 100km for the orbit to count. You have 5 minutes from launch.

Play the career contract tutorial 'Like a Bird'.
This tutorial covers the basics of building and flying airplanes with a very simple glider.
Contract Description: You've already tried to jump as far as possible from the runway; now you have to take off from it. Be wise and get some wings, or yolo it and find an alternative, you do you.

Play the career contract tutorial 'Droo Orbit'.
This tutorial covers staging analysis and tuning rocket engine performance in the designer, followed by a guided tutorial to achieve orbit around Droo.
Contract Description: Can you go to orbit? I need you near specific orbits and I know you can get there. First, reach any orbit to prove yourself.

Play the career contract tutorial 'Going High'.
This tutorial covers the basics of staging and payloads.
Contract Description: Droo's atmosphere ends right under 80km. Can you go to space to expose a probe a scientist sent me?

Play the career contract tutorial 'Learning To Fly'.
This tutorial guides you through a simple route to practice take off and landing.
Contract Description: This is a time trial for planes, so get your gloves tight! Go through all checkpoints in order before time runs out.

Play the career contract tutorial 'The Jump'.
This tutorial teaches the basics of building and driving a very simple wheeled ground vehicle.
Contract Description: One advantage of a huge ramp on a cliff's edge is you can fly without much effort. Go airborne for more than 150m after jumping from the end of the runway.

Play the career contract tutorial 'Vertical Shot'.
This tutorial teaches the basics of building and launching a simple rocket, and briefly covers the flight user interface.
Contract Description: When you send your fireworks high enough, hitting a house in the village can become a huge problem, but going too far makes finding the scraps annoying. Crash no further than 20km, but no closer than 500m from the launchpad.
