trans-unit.source: Activates the next stage in the craft.
Returns the status of the activation group. True indicates the AG is active.
Breaks out of a while or repeat loop.
Sends a message with the specified data to all matching receive message events in this program.
Sends a message with the specified data to all matching receive message events in all nearby crafts, consuming some energy based on the message size.
Sends a message with the specified data to all matching receive message events in this craft.
Event called when the craft enters a planet's sphere of influence.
Changes the value of the number variable by the specified amount.
This instruction does not execute and can be used to place comments in your program to help explain how it works.
Empty instruction that does not execute so you can place comments in your program.
Evaluates the condition and returns the specified result.
Returns true if the text on the left contains the text on the right.
Gets a property of the craft with the specified ID.
Event called when this craft docks with another craft. NOTE: Part IDs may change after docking with another craft.
The ID of the first craft found with the specified name, or -1 if none are found. If no name is provided, returns the ID of the craft running the program.
Creates the MFD widget of the specified type with the specified name.
Destroys the MFD widget with the specified name.
Displays the message at the top of the screen.
Only executes if all previous if/else if blocks were false. Must follow an if or else if block.
Only executes if previous if/else if blocks were false and this condition is true. Must follow an if or else if block.

Evaluates an input expression in this part's context. Time-based functions may be inaccurate if the input is evaluated at different intervals — for better results, create an InputController and reference its value from Vizzy.
Event called when the craft enters the flight scene for the first time.
Logs the message to the flight log. If the second parameter is true, it overrides the message; if false, it writes a new one every time.
Loops from the starting value to the end value by the step and provides a local variable 'i' with the current value.
Advanced formatting that uses C#'s built-in System.String method. Refer to Microsoft's documentation for more information.
Formats a value of a specified unit to user friendly text.
Variable that can change its value.
Only executes the code if the condition is true.
Returns the result of joining the two or more strings of text together.
Returns the length of the string of text.
Returns the letter at the specified location.
Adds the item to the end of the list.
Removes all items in the list.
Creates a new list from a list of comma separated values.
Gets the item in the list at the index. Index 1 is the first item in the list.
Gets the item's index in the list. Index 1 is the first item. If the item isn't in the list, 0 is returned.
Initializes the list with a set of comma separated values.
Inserts the item at the index in the list. Index 1 is the first item in the list.
Returns the length of the list.
Removes the item at the index from the list. Index 1 is the first item in the list.
Reverses the order of the items in the list.
Sets the item at the index in the list. If the list has no item at that index, nothing is set. Index 1 is the first item in the list.
Sorts the items in the list in ascending order.
Variable that can hold a list of items.
Locks the nav sphere on the specified indicator.
Locks the nav sphere on the specified vector in PCI coordinates.
Logs the message to the output log in the part running this program, viewable by clicking View Log in the part's inspector panel during flight.
Gets the frequency of the note at the octave.
Adds the left and right numbers together and returns the result.
Returns true if both sides are true.
Returns the angle in radians between the positive x-axis and the ray to the point.
Divides the left number by the right number and returns the result.
Returns true if both sides are equal.
Raises the left number to the power specified on the right side.
Returns true if the left number is greater than the right number.
Returns true if the left number is greater than or equal to the right number.
Returns true if the left number is less than the right number.
Returns true if the left number is less than or equal to the right number.
Returns the result of running the math function on the specified number. Math functions such as sin, cos, and tan expect the angle to be in radians.
Returns the larger of the two numbers.
Returns the smaller of the two numbers.
Returns the remainder of the left number divided by the right number.
Multiplies the left and right numbers together and returns the result.
Returns true if the condition is false. Returns false if the condition is true.
Returns true if either side is true.
Returns a random number between the two numbers.
Subtracts the right number from the left number and returns the result.
Gets a property of the part with the specified ID.
Event called when a part in the craft has collided with something else.
Event called when a part in the craft explodes.
The ID of the first part found with the specified name or -1 if none are found.
Converts the vector between local and PCI coordinates.
Gets a property of the specified planet.
Converts the position vector to a (latitude, longitude, AGL) vector.
Converts the position vector to a (latitude, longitude, ASL) vector. It is much faster than the AGL counterpart.
Converts the (latitude, longitude, AGL) vector to a position vector.
Converts the (latitude, longitude, ASL) vector to a position vector. It is much faster than the AGL counterpart.
Plays a beep sound with the specified parameters.
Plays a beep with the selected waveform, pitch, volume, and duration.
Returns the craft's current value for the specified input. The value returned will be between -1 and 1.
Gets the message name to broadcast when the widget receives the input.
Returns information about the MFD gauge with the specified name.
Returns information about the MFD label widget with the specified name.
Converts the position vector between a widget's local coordinate system and the display's global coordinate system.
Returns information about the MFD sprite with the specified name.
Gets the pixel at the specified coordinates. Note: Coordinates start at 1, not 0.
Gets the alpha value of the pixel at the specified coordinates (0 = transparent, 1 = opaque). Note: Coordinates start at 1, not 0.
Returns information about the MFD widget with the specified name.
Returns the current name of the selected item.
Returns the specified navigation property of the craft.
Returns the performance property of the craft.
Returns the specified time in seconds.
Returns the specified velocity in m/s (or m/s2 for accelerations).
Called when the flight program receives a message, with its data set to the value that was broadcasted.
Repeats the block of code the number of times specified.
Activates or deactivates the specified activation group. Setting an AG to true activates it. False deactivates it.
Sets the property on the camera.
Sets the pitch or heading the craft should target.
Sets the selected craft input to the specified amount. Value must be between -1 and 1. For example, to set throttle to 65%, set this to 0.65.
Sets alignment of the label's text.
Sets where the widget is anchored to its parent.

Sets the message name to broadcast when the widget receives the input. The message includes a data list: the first element is the data specified here, the second is the widget name, and the third is the local position of the input relative to the widget.
Sets the property of MFD gauge widget with the specified name.
Sets the property of MFD text widget with the specified name.
Sets the property of the line widget.
Sets the line widget to connect the first point to the second point.
Sets the property of MFD map widget with the specified name.
Sets the property of MFD navball widget with the specified name.
Sends the widget behind the target widget, or behind everything if the target widget does not exist. Note: Widgets must share the same parent.
Brings the widget in front of the target widget, or in front of all widgets if the target doesn't exist. Note: Widgets must share the same parent.
Sets the property of MFD sprite widget with the specified name.
Initializes the texture to the specified width and height.
Sets the pixel at the coordinate to the specified color and alpha (0 = transparent, 1 = opaque). Note: Coordinates start at 1, not 0.
Sets the property of MFD widget with the specified name.
Sets the property of the part with the specified ID.
Sets the craft's current target planet or craft.
Sets the current time mode of the game.
Sets the value of the variable.
Speaks the text aloud. Pitch is in Hz and duration is in seconds; pass 0 on either for the default.
Returns the letters of the text between the start and end locations. If 0 is specified for start/end then the start/end of the text will be used.
Switches to the craft with the specified ID. If the craft is far away, then this program may stop executing.
Gets information about the current planet's terrain at the specified (latitude, longitude, 0) vector. The z component of the vector is not used.
Sets the value of the variable to text received from an input dialog presented to the user with the specified message.
Creates a vector from the x, y, and z components.
Returns the result of the operation between the two vectors.
Converts a hexadecimal color (ie #FF0000) into a color vector (ie 1,0,0).
Waits the specified number of seconds. It's also recommended to place a wait at the end of while and repeat loops, as it can improve performance.
Waits until the condition is true.
Loops until its condition is no longer true.
